title: A Spectral Representation of Networks: The Path of Subgraphs

problem.claim: Spectral moments can capture network structure and graph properties, but networks with different structures or sizes may have the same or similar spectral moments.

gap.claim: Existing spectral information does not adequately distinguish all networks, including cospectral graphs.

contributions.claim: A 3D network representation called the Spectral Path connects the spectral moments of a network with those of its subgraphs of different sizes.
The Spectral Path is presented as interpretable and supported by a theoretical foundation for relating a network to its subgraphs.
The Spectral Path is applied to network visualization and network identification.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the Spectral Path is interpretable and provide a theoretical foundation.
The authors report effectiveness in network visualization and network identification applications.

narrative_sequence.summary: Network representation learning is important for studying networks.
Spectral analysis studies graphs through eigenvalue distributions, and spectral moments can encode network structure and graph properties.
Different networks may share similar spectral moments, including cospectral graphs.
The paper proposes the Spectral Path, which connects network and subgraph spectral moments across subgraph sizes.
The authors describe interpretability and theoretical support, then report applications in visualization and network identification.

source_observation.claim: Network-level spectral moments may be insufficient to distinguish networks with different structures or sizes.

interpretation.claim: Representations can become more discriminative by incorporating spectral information from subgraphs of different sizes.

application.claim: A subgraph-aware spectral representation may support network visualization and identification.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how broadly the representation resolves spectral ambiguities.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the construction details of the Spectral Path.
The abstract omits datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results.
The abstract does not detail the theoretical foundation or its assumptions.
